subject: Request: deterministic tail/ token-based throughput guarantees for Dedicated pool
messages:
From: Alex Tucker <alex.tucker@sabletech.io>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 27 Jun 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Deterministic tail guarantees + reserved GPU behaviour (SableTech RFP)

Hi Soojin,

Thanks again for the demo this week — SableTech's infra team reviewed Redwood's Dedicated offering and we have a couple of hard requirements to proceed through procurement. Our legal team asked me to collate them into a short RFP addendum (attached). High-level asks: 

- Deterministic tail-latency guarantees for inference calls under reserved GPU pool (95th/99th token latency SLAs).
- A token-based throughput floor (tokens per second) that is reserved regardless of noisy neighbors — we need guaranteed throughput for peak batch inference windows.
- Clear preemption semantics: how does Redwood evict/soft-preempt jobs on dedicated SKU during high cluster pressure; we need guaranteed limits on preemption frequency and a remediation credit mechanism.

Can Redwood provide a short draft addendum that maps these asks to service terms (we prefer explicit numeric commitments or fallback compensations)? Also keen to know whether queueing behavior during maintenance windows can be scoped to a carveout.

Thanks — attaching the RFP PDF. If useful, happy to do a 30-min call early next week to walk through.

Alex
Alex Tucker
Head of Infrastructure, SableTech
procurement@sabletech.io
Attachment: SLA_RFP_v2.pdf (application/pdf, 220KB)

From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
To: Alex Tucker <alex.tucker@sabletech.io>
Date: Sat, 27 Jun 2026 10:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Deterministic tail guarantees + reserved GPU behaviour (SableTech RFP)

Alex —

Appreciate the clear ask and the RFP. I'll loop in Ben (sales) and Marissa (CS/SLAs) to draft an addendum and quantify what we can commit to on Dedicated. Quick answers up front:

- We can propose deterministic tail targets for token-latency under a specific reservation profile and workload profile (we'll need their p95/p99 targets and representative prompt length/shape).
- Token-based throughput floors are doable as a contractual reservation (tokens/sec or tokens/minute) but the numeric mapping depends on model family, quantization, and batching policies.
- Preemption is normally rare for Dedicated pools; we have soft-preemption windows and a documented crediting model. We can propose tighter preemption caps for reserved SKUs with defined remediation credits.

Next steps: Ben — can you confirm the standard uplift/price for a deterministic tail addendum and whether legal has a templated carveout? Marissa — can you sketch the observability hooks we'd expose (token-level telemetry and queueing metrics) to verify compliance?

Alex — are you available Mon 6/29 11:00–11:30 PT for a sync?

Best,
Soojin
Soojin Lee

Subject: Fwd: Deterministic tail guarantees + reserved GPU behaviour (SableTech RFP)
CC: 

Ben / Marissa — forwarding SableTech RFP. Key asks summarized below (they attached PDF):

1) Deterministic p95/p99 token latency guarantees for Dedicated pool. They expect hard numbers (ms/token) or a numeric SLA with credits.
2) Token-based throughput floor (tokens/s) guaranteed irrespective of other tenants.
3) Explicit preemption limits (max events per week/month) + a crediting/remediation model.
4) Carveout for maintenance windows so critical peak jobs are not impacted.

Notes: Their workload is a mix of chat-style prompts (avg 600 tokens, bursts up to 50 concurrent requests) during a scheduled daily processing window. They flagged that quantization and batching materially change the token/sec mapping — they want the contract to call out model family (e.g., rwd-xt-2.7b-quant) and the expected quantization profile.

Please:
- Ben: propose commercial terms (price uplift, minimum commitment) and an initial numeric mapping for tokens/sec -> reserved GPU count for our common SKUs.
- Marissa: propose the verification signal set (token-level metrics, queue depth, preemption logs) and a candidate wording for maintenance carveout.

I'll schedule a 30-min with Alex on Mon 6/29 11am PT unless you tell me another slot.

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Alex Tucker <alex.tucker@sabletech.io>
Date: Mon, 29 Jun 2026 17:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Deterministic tail guarantees + reserved GPU behaviour (SableTech RFP)

Thanks for the flag, Soojin —

We can move on this and I'm attaching a working draft addendum (draft_sla_addendum_v1.docx) so SableTech has something concrete to review. Summary of our proposed approach:

- Deterministic tail-latency: Offer p95/p99 commitments expressed as ms per token for a specified "reservation profile" (model family + quantization + batch size). Example: rwd-xt-2.7b-quant, batch_size=8, guarantees: p95 <= 18ms/token, p99 <= 40ms/token for workloads matching their provided prompt distribution.

- Token-based throughput floor: Contract will specify a reserved tokens-per-minute number (e.g., 1.8M tokens/min) mapped to a guaranteed pool size. We'll include an explicit conversion table in the addendum that maps tokens/min -> reserved GPU count by model family and quantization.

- Preemption & remediation: Propose a cap of 2 soft-preemptions per 30-day window per tenant for Dedicated reservations; any excess triggers a service credit equal to X% of monthly committed spend (see draft wording). Hard preemptions for emergency maintenance are excluded but require 48-hour notice and a targeted credit calculation.

- Maintenance carveout: We propose a scoped carveout for scheduled maintenance windows (max 4 hours/month) where the token-floor may be temporarily reduced but we will offer advance notifications and alternate scheduling options during their daily peak window. Unscheduled events will follow remediation pathways above.

Marissa — can you validate the telemetry set? Specifically we should expose:
- token_throughput (tokens/sec) at tenant aggregate
- p95_token_latency_ms, p99_token_latency_ms
- queue_depth_inflight, preemption_events (timestamped)

If that looks good I'll ask legal to start fast-tracking a slim addendum and pricing ops to generate uplift quotes. Alex — if this sounds reasonable, let's confirm the call at Mon 6/29 11:00 PT.

Ben Carter
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
